items.summary: The Madras High Court has constituted a five-member board of management headed by two retired High Court judges to take over the administration of the Chidambaram Nataraja Temple [Sabanayagar Temple Vs State of TN]. A Division Bench of Justices G Jayachandran and E Manoharan passed the order after finding maladministration, damage to heritage structures and failure to properly account for temple properties. The Court held that judicial intervention was necessary to address the irregularities in the management of the temple by the Podhu Dikshitars, a religious denomination constitutionally entitled to administer its affairs. Interestingly, the order was passed on a petition filed by Podhu Dikshitars themselves who moved the Court taking objection to a government order permitting devotees to climb atop a Mandapam for the darshan of the temple deity. " Therefore, we constitute a Board of Management consisting of domain experts, who will take over the administration, till the ill is cured, " the Court said. items.title: Transparency on trial: Mapping courts’ compliance with the RTI Act
items.summary: The effectiveness of the Right to Information (RTI) regime has, in recent years, come under a cloud of uncertainty with commentators pointing at a progressive weakening of RTI mechanisms. Among the concerns are onerous delays in appointments of information commissioners and other officials, rising backlogs and arbitrary rejections of requests by public authorities . The amendment effected to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 further exacerbated these concerns as it empowered public authorities to deny information if it qualified as ‘personal information’, without requiring it to be weighed against public interest. While the High Courts and the Supreme Court often find themselves adjudicating upon the failure of government ministries and departments to comply with the RTI Act, the courts themselves are guilty of not adhering to the principles of the Act. The 2024-25 Annual Report of the Central Information Commission (CIC) reveals that among all public authorities in the country, the Delhi High Court has the highest rate of rejection of RTI applications followed by the Supreme Court.
